final_message:
**Status:** Reproduced (Linux, Node 24.19.0, eslint at 35cf44c, reports itself as 9.30.1). The reporter was on Windows; the failing code path is the same on both.

- **Expected:** `eslint <dir> --fix` writes the fix to every file and exits 0.
- **Actual:** ESLint crashes with exit code 2 and leaves files partly fixed (1003 of 1025):
  ```
  Error: EMFILE: too many open files, open '.../tmp/emfile-fix-check/file_98.js'
      at async open (node:internal/fs/promises:697:25)
      at async Object.writeFile (node:internal/fs/promises:1317:14)
      at async Promise.all (index 1003)
      at async ESLint.outputFixes (lib/eslint/eslint.js:533:3)
      at async Object.execute (lib/cli.js:637:4)
      at async main (bin/eslint.js:175:19)
  ```
  This is the same stack as in the report.
- **Trigger:** more files with autofixes than the open-file limit (`ulimit -n` + 1). Linting itself passes, because file reads already retry on EMFILE. The crash happens only when the fixes are written to disk.
- **Run:** `bash -c 'ulimit -n 1024 && node tools/check-emfile-handling-fix.js'`. It takes a few seconds and exits 1 when the bug reproduces.
- **Reliability:** failed 3 out of 3 runs at a limit of 1024. It also failed once at this machine's default limit (524288 files, about 7 minutes), so the low limit only makes it faster and isn't what causes the crash.
- **Artifacts:** a new script, `tools/check-emfile-handling-fix.js`. It copies the existing EMFILE check (`npm run test:emfile`), but every generated file has a problem `eol-last` can fix, and it runs `--fix --no-config-lookup --rule "eol-last: [error, always]"`. Afterwards it counts how many files were fixed and checks whether the error came from `outputFixes`. As a baseline, the unchanged `tools/check-emfile-handling.js` passes at the same limit.

**Likely cause:** in `lib/eslint/eslint.js` lines 533–545, `ESLint.outputFixes` starts one `fs.writeFile` per fixed file all at once with `Promise.all`. Those writes have no retry and no limit on how many run at a time, unlike the read path, which uses `@humanwhocodes/retry`.

I didn't change any production code.
